newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian privatization rules limit CVRD consortia.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian privatization rules limit CVRD consortia.

text.p: Restrictions on large iron ore producers, traders and buyers in the privatization auction of Brazilian state mining company CVRD are limiting the number of bidding consortia, according to Anglo-Australian mining group RTZ-CRA.
Under the CVRD privatization rules, large iron ore producers like RTZ-CRA, as well as large traders and buyers, can only hold a 10 percent stake in any consortium bidding for CVRD.
A 45 percent block of CVRD voting shares is being auctioned on April 29 for three billion reais ($2.83 billion).

"When the government imposed these restrictions, it took the risk of alienating many big players," said Julio Carvalho, the financial director of RTZ-CRA's Brazil unit. "Three (consortia) is unlikely. There will be one or two."

RTZ-CRA has been linked in the Brazilian press to a consortium that includes Japan's Mitsui & Co, Australian mining firm WMC Ltd and iron ore miner MBR, which is owned by Brazilian metals and mining group Caemi, but Carvalho denied there were any ties.

"We have not made up our mind whether to participate in the auction or not. We are waiting to see what offers might come our way. We are talking to everyone," Carvalho said. "It is fairly uninteresting because we are restricted to a 10 percent participation."

Carvalho said a consortium based on shared control in which all participants had equal say regardless of their actual stake would be more attractive to firms like RTZ-CRA, but such an arrangement was difficult to implement legally.
Brazil's largest steelmaker, Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN), which is looking to lead another consortium in the CVRD auction, is also a strong advocate of shared control.

"The precondition for our consortium is a power equilibrium, or shared control," said Maria Silvia Bastos Marques, director of CSN's corporate sector. "We are not going to join a consortium in which we have no say."
CSN's efforts to form a consortium suffered recently when two potential partners, Brazilian retail bank Bradesco and South Africa's Gencor Ltd dropped out.

Bradesco cannot participate in any consortium bidding for CVRD because it is a member of the consultative group evaluating CVRD for privatization. Gencor issued a statement that it was no longer interested in pursuing a bid.
But CSN has not been detered from participating in the CVRD auction, according to CSN spokesman Francisco Padilha.
"CSN is absolutely determined to participate in the auction," he said. "We have sufficient funding to see this through to the end."
Bradesco continued to support the CSN bid from outside the consortium and Gencor was not completely disinterested, but was looking for only a minor role.
Padilha said CSN was also talking with other interested parties such as Japan's Nippon Steel Corp.
"We are talking to everyone," Padilha said.

But the Japanese steelmaker has also been negotiating with another potential consortium including Brazil's metals, cement and pulp group Votorantim, South Africa's Anglo American Corp and Banco Safra.
